summary: The diff implements all three requirements with reasonable coverage. REQ-1 (admin bootstrap) is addressed via frontend token passing and backend adminInitialized flag. REQ-2 (CommunityPost media blobs) is addressed in backend/main.mo with updated types and a migration module. REQ-3 (frontend media upload form) is addressed in Community.tsx and CommunityPostCard.tsx. However, the backend implementation of REQ-1 relies on a hardcoded token passed from the frontend rather than pure backend bootstrap logic, and the diff does not show the backend saveCallerUserProfile function body confirming the no-admin-exists-yet logic. Some acceptance criteria cannot be fully confirmed due to truncation.

missing_requirements.requirement: If no admin exists yet when a new user profile is created, that user should be promoted to Admin without requiring any manual token claim — the backend should check if any admin exists and auto-promote.
missing_requirements.reason: The implementation passes a hardcoded admin token from the frontend (FIRST_USER_ADMIN_TOKEN in useQueries.ts) to saveCallerUserProfile. This means admin promotion still depends on a token claim mechanism rather than pure backend-side detection of no admin existing yet. The backend main.mo is truncated so the saveCallerUserProfile body is not visible to confirm backend-side auto-detection logic.

hallucinated_features.description: A blob-storage abstraction layer with ExternalBlob type and getDirectURL() methods was introduced, suggesting blobs are served via URLs rather than being purely stored within the backend actor.
hallucinated_features.reason: The build request explicitly constrains that all blob/media storage must remain within the Motoko backend actor with no external storage services. The migration module and main.mo both import blob-storage/Storage and blob-storage/Mixin modules, and the frontend CommunityPostCard uses getDirectURL() on ExternalBlob objects, which implies blobs are accessed via URLs from an external-like storage layer rather than being purely inlined in the actor state.
